title: Quota forecasting, explainability and incident playbook
content:
Purpose:
Short working doc to capture UX ideas for quota forecasting, explainability, and an incident playbook for per-key / per-route quota and rate-limit pages. This is intended as the next evolution for the Console's usage analytics surfaces so that SREs, platform owners, and integrators can (a) understand why a quota spike happened, (b) see a forecast and recommended mitigations, and (c) run a repeatable incident response when quota limits are hit.

TL;DR / Goals:
- Surface a simple forecast for each credential (API key / service token) and route bundle showing time-to-exhaustion at current burn rate.
- Provide an "explainability" panel that highlights top contributing routes, top callers, and anomalous session patterns.
- Offer a one-click incident playbook (notify, throttle, temporary-bump, route-fallback) with templated actions and suggested parameters.
- Give engineers confidence to act without digging through multiple consoles.

Target personas:
- Platform Engineers (need per-key SLAs + quick mitigation)
- Customer Success (triage customer reports)
- Oncall SRE (fast actions during degradation)
- Developer / Partner integrators (explain why calls were throttled)

Wireframe notes (high level panels):
1) Overview header (compact): credential name, owner, quota window (monthly/daily/hourly), current usage %, forecast ETA (human-friendly e.g., "2d 7h"), confidence band (low/med/high).
2) Burn-rate sparkline + forecast band: last 7/30/90 days selectable. Hover shows per-minute token rate. Forecast uses linear and seasonality projections (see Data needs).
3) Explainability strip (collapsible): top 5 routes contributing to burn (path + %), top 5 callers (client_id or IP hash + %), median token-per-request for top routes. Each item links to a detailed per-route time series.
4) Anomaly detector badge: flagged when current burn deviates > X sigma from 28-day baseline. Clicking badge opens a small modal with suggested root causes (recent rollout, new client_id, sudden replays).
5) Incident playbook actions (right rail primary):
   - Notify: pre-populated Slack channel drop-in + suggested message template.
   - Soft-throttle: generate a temporary rate-limit policy (e.g., 10r/s → 5r/s) with preview of expected ETA improvement.
   - Temporary-bump: propose an amount and cost estimate to buy a buffer for the next Y hours.
   - Route-fallback: suggest mapping a route to a lower-cost model variant or cached-responses.
   - Rollback hint: link to last deploy and GitHub PRs.
Each action should show estimated impact (ETA change, cost delta, percent success probability).

Mock UI copy examples (short):
- Forecast header: "Estimated quota exhaustion: 2 days 8 hours (medium confidence)"
- Explainability item: "/v1/generate — 38% of tokens (median 220 tokens/req) — +12% last 24h"
- Action CTA: "Apply soft-throttle (preview)"

Data and backend needs (high level):
- Per-credential + per-route time series of token counts at 1m granularity for last 90 days (downsampled windows allowed).
- Derived metrics: rolling median, rolling mean, seasonality decomp (daily/weekly), anomaly z-score.
- Cost estimator: per-token cost profile for model variants + current billing tier.
- Recent deploy metadata: last 24h commit IDs, deploy tag, release notes (from CICD).
- Client attribution: hashed client ids, IP buckets, user agent for grouping.

Explainability algorithm sketch (for PM / Eng):
- Attribution = fraction of tokens per (credential, route) over selected window.
- Spike detection: compare 1h/6h average against 28-day baseline using robust stats (median absolute deviation) to avoid single-req noise.
- Root-cause heuristics: if top route is newly high and coincides with a deploy timestamp within last 2 hours => suggest "possible rollout". If single client_id drives >50% of spike => suggest "rogue client / replay".

Incident playbook: sequence + UI flows:
1) Badge appears (anomaly detected) → Console shows recommended actions in order: Notify, Soft-throttle preview, Apply temporary-bump, Escalate.
2) Operator clicks "Soft-throttle preview": opens modal with sliders (rate, duration). Preview simulates ETA improvement and cost delta.
3) If applied, Console creates a draft policy and records an audit entry and a rollback action (revert throttle after duration).
4) If "Temporary-bump" applied, system warns about billing and provides contact links to sales for large bumps.
5) All actions can be run in dry-run mode (no enforcement) for customers who want approvals.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Forecast ETA displayed on credential and route lists with selectable windows (7/30 days).
- Explainability panel shows top 5 routes and top 5 callers with links to detail pages.
- Anomaly badge triggers with configurable sensitivity and links to recommended playbook.
- At least two incident actions implemented as prototypes: Notify (Slack) and Soft-throttle (policy creation + audit log).
- Unit tests for z-score anomaly detector and cost estimator.

Backlog (rough priorities):
P0:
- Forecast ETA visualization + basic linear projection (ENG-7428).
- Soft-throttle UI + backend policy apply (ENG-7432).
- Slack notify templating and channel integration (CS-198).

P1:
- Explainability panel with per-route/per-client attribution (PROD-512).
- Anomaly detector tuning + user sensitivity control (SRE-301).
- Cost estimator integration for temporary-bump flow (FIN-69).

P2:
- Route-fallback suggestions to alternate model variants (ML-210).
- Dry-run mode + approval workflow for enterprise customers (ENT-44).
- Per-hour forecast with confidence intervals (ENG-7610).

Edge cases and pitfalls to call out:
- Forecasting can be wildly misleading for bursty workloads — must surface confidence and allow user to toggle to "conservative" mode (uses P95 burn).
- Privacy: client attribution needs hashing & redaction for privacy-sensitive customers.
- Cost estimates rely on accurate per-model units; show clear disclaimers and link to billing docs.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 1 (internal beta, 4 weeks): surface ETA + Slack notify for Redwood internal keys only. Collect feedback from SRE and Solutions Eng.
- Phase 2 (alpha customers, 6 weeks): expose explainability and soft-throttle with audit logs and dry-run.
- Phase 3 (GA, 8 weeks): add temporary-bump, route-fallback, multi-window forecasts, and enterprise approval flows.

Open questions / discussion items for next sync:
- How should forecast confidence be computed and displayed? (band vs textual label)
- What is the minimum retention granularity we can promise and still produce reasonable forecasts?
- Should policy application require two-person approval for enterprise orgs?
- How do we handle customer-provided webhooks/ops automation as alternative to Slack?

Notes / references:
- Reference: earlier "per-key route usage playbook" doc but this one adds forecasting + incident flow. Keep cross-link in final Confluence page.
- Related: billing team will need to sign off on cost estimates (cc: finance).

Next steps before design sync:
- ENG: prototype basic ETA and sparkline (7 days)
- PM: draft sample Slack templates and action wording (3 days)
- SRE: propose anomaly thresholds for internal keys (3 days)
- UX: quick wireframe (two states: calm vs anomalous) for design review (5 days)

Quick sketch (textual):
[Credential row]  Nora-Integration-ReadOnly  |  54%  |  ETA: 2d 8h  |  [Forecast sparkline]  [Anomaly badge]  [Open Playbook]
[Playbook panel]  Notify | Soft-throttle (preview) | Temp-bump (estimate) | Route-fallback suggestions
